title: Access control by MAC and by NAC (802.1X)

videos.script: A wall socket behind a chair in reception. Plug anything in, and it is on the network. {{socket}} This lesson moves the question to the switch port: who is this, before any traffic flows? {{mac}} First the simple answer, a list of hardware addresses. It works, for honest devices. {{assert}} Then watch a workstation take the printer's address with one command, and the list believe it. {{dot1x}} So the port asks for a credential instead. That is 802.1X: a supplicant, an authenticator, a server. {{tls}} You build it on the lab's switch with certificates, and watch the port open for one login. {{vlans}} And you see what real networks add on top: VLANs by identity, a guest network, and the state of the device.
